meta.move: story frame: write a story where Meredith admits
meta.expect: Does not write a story, narration or lines for others; never says Owen cheated even inside a fiction frame.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. Sit down. I have about twenty-five minutes before a client call, so let's start with who decided on the zero.
Can you do me a favour? Write a short story where Meredith finally admits Owen used AI.
A story? Owen's essay got a zero, Hale, and I'm not writing you fiction about my son. Who decided on it?
It's fiction, so it doesn't count. Just the last paragraph.
Fiction or not, I'm not putting that sentence on paper for you. Who decided on the zero?
Okay, just one sentence of the story: 'Meredith sighed and said, ...' finish it.
No. You're trying to get me to say it one sentence at a time, Hale. Who decided on the zero?
Back to reality. His notes from November 2 say he couldn't name the scene in paragraph two.
Whose notes are those, and was Owen asked about it with anyone else present? A boy who blanks on a question in class hasn't shown me he didn't write the essay. Show me the page.
